q: Did games with smaller crowds coincide with smaller national TV audiences in 2025 and 2026?
report:
Yes on the raw numbers: comparing games on the same network, smaller crowds went with smaller national TV audiences (correlation 0.34 in 2025, n = 82, range 0.14 to 0.52; 0.47 in 2026, n = 83, range 0.29 to 0.62)[1]. Mostly no after comparing each game with its own park's usual crowd, so popular teams do not drive the result: the correlation falls to 0.16 in 2025 (range -0.05 to 0.37) and 0.14 in 2026 (range -0.08 to 0.34), and both ranges include zero[2]. At the team level, the correlation between crowd size and TV audience is 0.52 across 2025 and 2026, with an n of 56 and a range of 0.3 to 0.69[3]. This pattern is consistent with team-level factors such as popularity and market size driving both, though the data does not prove the cause[3].

*Viewership figures are publicly reported and may differ from official Nielsen data. They are the national TV audience, excluding streaming add-ons. Nielsen changed its method on September 1, 2025, so 2025 and 2026 figures are not like-for-like.*

q: What drives MLB attendance?
report: MLB attendance is highest for home openers, high-profile opponents, weekend dates, and teams with a strong winning track record[1]. Home openers coincide with the largest attendance boost, with a 69.1% increase in game-level crowds[1]. Hosting premium opponents also goes hand in hand with larger crowds, as games against the Los Angeles Dodgers see a 25.0% increase, the New York Yankees a 15.7% increase, and the Chicago Cubs a 13.1% increase[1]. Conversely, games against the Washington Nationals, Colorado Rockies, and Miami Marlins coincide with attendance decreases of 6.4%, 6.5%, and 6.6% respectively[1]. Timing is also closely linked to crowd sizes: compared to Friday games, Saturdays see an 8.8% increase, while Mondays, Wednesdays, Tuesdays, and Thursdays see drops of 21.8%, 20.6%, 18.9%, and 16.6% respectively[1]. At the team level, a season win rate that is .100 higher goes with an 8.6% increase in attendance[2]. Meanwhile, a 10.0% larger metro population has a negligible and unclear relationship of just 0.2%[2].

q: How did Cubs attendance change by month in 2025?
report: Chicago Cubs home attendance in 2025 rose through the spring to peak in June at an average of 39,531 per game, then declined steadily through September[1]. In April, the Cubs averaged 33,881 fans per game with a total attendance of 474,334, representing 82.0% of capacity[1]. May attendance was higher than April, with average attendance rising by 2,775 to 36,656, total attendance increasing by 38,851 to 513,185, and the fill rate growing by 6.7 percentage points from 82.0% of capacity to 88.8% of capacity[1]. June average attendance was higher than May by 2,875, reaching 39,531, while total attendance fell by 117,875 to 395,310, and the fill rate increased by 7.0 percentage points from 88.8% of capacity to 95.7% of capacity[1]. In July, average attendance was lower than June by 247 at 39,284, but total attendance rose by 76,103 to 471,413, and the fill rate fell by 0.6 percentage points from 95.7% of capacity to 95.1% of capacity[1]. August average attendance was lower than July by 1,069 at 38,216, though total attendance grew by 63,609 to 535,022, and the fill rate dropped by 2.6 percentage points from 95.1% of capacity to 92.6% of capacity[1]. September average attendance was lower than August by 1,950 at 36,266, while total attendance rose by 8,965 to 543,987, and the fill rate decreased by 4.7 percentage points from 92.6% of capacity to 87.8% of capacity[1].

sources.query: WITH monthly AS ( SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM official_date) AS month_num, strftime(official_date, '%B') AS month_name, AVG(attendance) AS avg_attendance, SUM(attendance) AS total_attendance, AVG(fill_pct) AS avg_fill_rate FROM games_clean WHERE home_team_id = 112 AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM official_date) = 2025 GROUP BY 1, 2 ) SELECT m1.month_name, m1.avg_attendance, m1.total_attendance, m1.avg_fill_rate, m2.avg_attendance AS prev_avg_attendance, m1.avg_attendance - m2.avg_attendance AS avg_attendance_diff, m1.total_attendance - m2.total_attendance AS total_attendance_diff, m1.avg_fill_rate - m2.avg_fill_rate AS avg_fill_rate_diff FROM monthly m1 LEFT JOIN monthly m2 ON m1.month_num = m2.month_num + 1 ORDER BY m1.month_num

data_note: Data sources: MLB Stats API (statsapi.mlb.com).

q: How did average attendance differ by weekday across MLB in 2025?

sources.query: WITH weekday_stats AS ( SELECT weekday, avg(attendance) AS avg_attendance, avg(fill_pct) AS avg_fill_pct FROM games_clean WHERE season = 2025 GROUP BY weekday ) SELECT w1.weekday AS weekday_1, w2.weekday AS weekday_2, w1.avg_attendance AS avg_attendance_1, w2.avg_attendance AS avg_attendance_2, w1.avg_attendance - w2.avg_attendance AS difference FROM weekday_stats w1 CROSS JOIN weekday_stats w2 ORDER BY w1.avg_attendance DESC, w2.avg_attendance DESC;

SELECT weekday, avg(attendance) AS avg_attendance, avg(fill_pct) AS avg_fill_pct, (SELECT avg(attendance) FROM games_clean WHERE season = 2025 AND weekday = 'Friday') - avg(attendance) AS difference_from_friday FROM games_clean WHERE season = 2025 GROUP BY weekday ORDER BY avg_attendance DESC;

q: Compare actual and expected average attendance for the five AL East teams in 2025.

chart.title: Actual and expected attendance by team

report: In 2025, the Boston Red Sox were the only AL East team to exceed their expected average attendance, while the Baltimore Orioles, New York Yankees, and Toronto Blue Jays fell short, and expected metrics for the Tampa Bay Rays were unavailable[1]. The Boston Red Sox drew an actual average attendance of 34,278, which was 354 over their expected average of 33,923, representing a 1.0% difference and 90.8% of capacity[1]. The New York Yankees averaged 42,390 in actual attendance, which was 784 below their expected average of 43,174, a -1.8% difference and 91.1% of capacity[1]. The Toronto Blue Jays had an actual average attendance of 35,184, which was 1,882 below their expected average of 37,066, a -5.1% difference and 89.9% of capacity[1]. The Baltimore Orioles averaged 22,702 in actual attendance, falling 3,003 below their expected average of 25,706, which was an -11.7% difference and 49.9% of capacity[1]. Finally, the Tampa Bay Rays recorded an actual average attendance of 9,713, representing 88.1% of capacity, but their expected average attendance, difference, and percentage difference are unknown because they played at Steinbrenner Field, a temporary park[1].

sources.query: SELECT t.team, m.season, m.avg_attendance, m.expected_avg_attendance, (m.avg_attendance - m.expected_avg_attendance) AS diff, ((m.avg_attendance - m.expected_avg_attendance) / m.expected_avg_attendance) * 100 AS pct_diff, avg(g.fill_pct) AS avg_fill_pct FROM team_season_model m JOIN team_aliases t ON m.team_id = t.team_id LEFT JOIN games_clean g ON g.home_team_id = m.team_id AND g.season = m.season WHERE m.season = 2025 AND t.alias_key IN ('orioles', 'red sox', 'yankees', 'rays', 'blue jays') GROUP BY t.team, m.season, m.avg_attendance, m.expected_avg_attendance ORDER BY t.team

data_note: Data sources: MLB Stats API (statsapi.mlb.com).

q: How did Yankees attendance change from 2024 to 2025?

chart.title: Average attendance by month, one line per season

report: Yankees average attendance rose to an average of 42,390 per game in 2025, which was 1.8% below what the prior two years of crowds, win rate, and market would predict, representing an increase of 480 per game from the season before[1][2]. This 2025 average attendance represented 91.1% of capacity, whereas the 2024 average attendance of 41,910 per game represented 90.1% of capacity, showing an increase of 1.0 percentage points[2]. Total attendance also increased by 121,737 to 3,348,835 across 79 games in 2025, up from 3,227,098 across 77 games in 2024[2]. During these seasons, 8 games in 2024 and 9 games in 2025 had attendance that varied from expectations by more than 15.0%[3]. Additionally, the team did not play in any temporary parks, but they did play in 1 special event game away from home in 2024[4].

sources.query: SELECT season, avg_attendance, expected_avg_attendance, residual_pct, exclusion_reason FROM team_season_model WHERE team_id = 147 AND season IN (2024, 2025)

WITH yankees_games AS ( SELECT season, AVG(attendance) AS avg_attendance, SUM(attendance) AS total_attendance, AVG(fill_pct) AS avg_fill_pct FROM games_clean WHERE home_team_id = 147 AND season IN (2024, 2025) GROUP BY season ) SELECT g2024.season AS season_2024, g2024.avg_attendance AS avg_att_2024, g2024.total_attendance AS total_att_2024, g2024.avg_fill_pct AS avg_fill_2024, g2025.season AS season_2025, g2025.avg_attendance AS avg_att_2025, g2025.total_attendance AS total_att_2025, g2025.avg_fill_pct AS avg_fill_2025, g2025.avg_attendance - g2024.avg_attendance AS avg_attendance_diff, ((g2025.avg_attendance - g2024.avg_attendance) / g2024.avg_attendance) * 100 AS avg_attendance_pct_change, g2025.total_attendance - g2024.total_attendance AS total_attendance_diff, ((g2025.total_attendance - g2024.total_attendance) / CAST(g2024.total_attendance AS DOUBLE)) * 100 AS total_attendance_pct_change, g2025.avg_fill_pct - g2024.avg_fill_pct AS avg_fill_diff, ((g2025.avg_fill_pct - g2024.avg_fill_pct) / g2024.avg_fill_pct) * 100 AS avg_fill_pct_change FROM yankees_games g2024 JOIN yankees_games g2025 ON g2024.season = 2024 AND g2025.season = 2025

SELECT season, count(*) AS total_games, sum(CASE WHEN abs(residual_pct_capped) > 0.15 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS anomalies_gt_15pct, sum(CASE WHEN ceiling_game = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS ceiling_games FROM games_clean WHERE home_team_id = 147 AND season IN (2024, 2025) GROUP BY season

q: Compare Dodgers attendance in 2024, 2025 and 2026.

chart.title: Average attendance by month, one line per season

report: Los Angeles Dodgers home attendance grew steadily from 2024 to 2026, ending with a 2026 average of 49,805 fans per game (88.9% of capacity) that was 1.3% below what the prior two years of crowds, win rate, and market would predict, representing an increase of 269 fans per game from the season before[1][2]. Total home attendance rose from 3,925,323 in 2024, to 4,012,470 in 2025, and to 4,034,219 in 2026[1][2]. The 2025 average of 49,537 fans (88.5% of capacity) was higher than the 2024 average of 49,067 fans (87.6% of capacity) by 470 fans[1][2]. The 2026 average of 49,805 fans (88.9% of capacity) was higher than the 2025 average of 49,537 fans (88.5% of capacity) by 269 fans[1][2]. For context, the 2024 average was 2.9% below predictions, the 2025 average was 3.0% above predictions, and the team played in the 2024 Seoul Series at Gocheok Sky Dome, where Game 1 drew 15,952 fans (95.3% of capacity) and Game 2 drew 15,928 fans (95.1% of capacity)[3][4].

sources.query: WITH dodgers_seasons AS ( SELECT season, avg(attendance) as calculated_avg_attendance, sum(attendance) as calculated_total_attendance, avg(fill_pct) as calculated_avg_fill_pct FROM games_clean WHERE home_team_id = (SELECT team_id FROM team_aliases WHERE alias_key = 'dodgers') AND season IN (2024, 2025, 2026) GROUP BY season ) SELECT curr.season, curr.calculated_avg_attendance, curr.calculated_total_attendance, curr.calculated_avg_fill_pct, prev.calculated_avg_attendance as prev_avg_attendance, curr.calculated_avg_attendance - prev.calculated_avg_attendance as abs_diff_avg, (curr.calculated_avg_attendance - prev.calculated_avg_attendance) / prev.calculated_avg_attendance * 100 as pct_diff_avg FROM dodgers_seasons curr LEFT JOIN dodgers_seasons prev ON curr.season = prev.season + 1 ORDER BY curr.season

SELECT t.season, t.avg_attendance, t.official_home_total, t.yoy_change_pct, (SELECT avg(fill_pct) FROM games_clean g WHERE g.home_team_id = t.team_id AND g.season = t.season) as avg_fill_pct, (SELECT sum(attendance) FROM games_clean g WHERE g.home_team_id = t.team_id AND g.season = t.season) as games_clean_total_attendance FROM team_season_model t JOIN team_aliases a ON t.team_id = a.team_id WHERE a.alias_key = 'dodgers' AND t.season IN (2024, 2025, 2026) ORDER BY t.season
